edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Inspice Liam, typum Synagogae fuisse; Tam infirmis oculis, quam Jacob in signo recepit: Et tamen servivit rursum pro minore dilecta. Mysterium verum et typum Ecclesiae nostrae. Intuite plene dictum Rebeccae de coelo: Unde similantes alienae, Christo credatis. Deinde Thamar partum geminorum adite: Ad Cain intendite, primum terrae cultorem, Et Abel pastorem, qui fuit immaculatus In fratris exitio offertor mactatus a fratre. Sic ergo percipite, juniores Christo probatos.
pass_a_gloss: Look at Leah, she was a type of the Synagogue; with eyes as weak as Jacob received her in a sign: And yet she served again for the less loved one. A true mystery and type of our Church. Look fully at the word spoken by Rebecca from heaven: From where you imitate strangers, you believe in Christ. Then approach the birth of Tamar's twins: Look at Cain, the first cultivator of the earth, And Abel the shepherd, who was immaculate, He was slain and offered in the destruction of his brother by his brother. So therefore understand, younger ones approved by Christ.
pass_b_english: Look at Leah: she was a type of the Synagogue, with eyes as weak as Jacob found her by sign; yet she served again for the less-loved wife (Genesis 29:17-18). It is a true mystery and type of our Church. Listen fully to the word spoken to Rebecca from heaven: from that source you imitate strangers, so that you may believe in Christ. Then consider Tamar's twin birth: look at Cain, the first tiller of the soil, and at Abel the shepherd, who was blameless, slain and offered up in his brother's murder by his own brother (Genesis 4:1-16). So then, you younger ones approved by Christ, understand this.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the necessary scripture citations (Genesis 29:17-18 and Genesis 4:1-16) for the allusions to Leah and the Cain/Abel narrative, which is required by the instructions. Pass A and B are consistent with the Latin source.
